title: Hybrid-order nonlinear topological phases
authors: Yu-Peng Ma, Ming-Jian Gao, Jun-Hong An
abstract: The bulk-boundary correspondence (BBC), which relates topological invariants to boundary modes, is well understood for linear systems but remains an open question in the presence of nonlinearity, where multigap topologies make the BBC obscure and the topological description troublesome. We address this by developing an auxiliary-system formalism that enables topological classification of nonlinear-eigenvalue systems. In the two-dimension (2D) case, we show that two fixed eigenvalues can harbor first-order gapless boundary modes and second-order corner modes. Stacking this 2D system along the third dimension (3D) reveals distinct hybrid-order realizations. Under uniform stacking, the corner states in the $xy$ plane transform into hinge states along the $z$ axis, yielding a 3D second-order phase, while the gapless boundary states become side-surface states, yielding a 3D first-order phase. For dimerized stacking, these states are further confined to the two ends of the $z$ axis, yielding a 3D third-order phase, and localized at the hinges, yielding a 3D second-order phase. Our results establish a multiband bulk-boundary correspondence and identify stacking engineering as a versatile platform for exploring hybrid-order topological phases in nonlinear systems.
summary: The paper tackles the challenge of applying bulk-boundary correspondence to complex nonlinear eigenvalue problems. By developing an auxiliary system formalism, it successfully classifies these systems and demonstrates how stacking a 2D model into 3D allows for the engineering of exotic hybrid-order topological phases (first-, second-, and third-order). This highlights stacking as a powerful tool for exploring nonlinearity in topology.
main_problem: The bulk-boundary correspondence (BBC) is poorly understood for nonlinear systems, especially those with multigap topologies, making topological description difficult.
main_result: The study establishes a multiband bulk-boundary correspondence and identifies stacking engineering as a versatile platform for realizing hybrid-order topological phases in nonlinear systems.
method: An auxiliary-system formalism is developed to map the nonlinear eigenvalue problem into a formally linear pencil matrix, allowing topological classification via spectral analysis.
model_or_system: The work analyzes a 2D spinless square-lattice model with two degrees of freedom per unit cell. This system is extended to 3D by stacking along the z-axis using SSH chain concepts.
key_observables: Topological invariants include Chern number ($C_1$) and mirror-graded winding number ($W_2$). State localization is diagnosed using the Inverse Participation Ratio (IPR).
important_parameters: Stacking parameters, such as those governing uniform vs. dimerized stacking, dictate the resulting order of the topological phase (first-, second-, or third-order).
main_assumptions: The method relies on mapping the nonlinear problem to a formally linear auxiliary system; it extends previous work limited to single-gap topologies.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the eigenvalue spectra under OBC and PBC, demonstrating the coexistence of first-order boundary states ($\omega=0$) and second-order corner states ($\omega=-M^{-1}$).
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the auxiliary system formalism for nonlinear BBC in 2D to analyzing how stacking this 2D structure into 3D yields distinct hybrid-order phases (e.g., uniform vs. dimerized stacking).
why_interesting: This work directly addresses the generalization of topological concepts (like BBC) from linear to nonlinear systems, which is a major frontier in condensed matter theory relevant to engineered quantum/photonic structures.
